### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-audit`, `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, touching **73** documentable anchor(s).

**68** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json cfe3563003933662ffc785e2b10041bb406551ce`.

⛔ **15** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `userId (5 routes)`
- **2** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `objectName (symbol, 57 pages)`, `created_at (literal, 43 pages)`
- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **26** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json cfe3563003933662ffc785e2b10041bb406551ce` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `6066ba3171b58b3401a078fc8832999e8933996f` — the merge of head `03f6f67180e155035fef8fbedd625e19364e1ac0` into base `cfe3563003933662ffc785e2b10041bb406551ce`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 6066ba3171b58b3401a078fc8832999e8933996f && git checkout 6066ba3171b58b3401a078fc8832999e8933996f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin cfe3563003933662ffc785e2b10041bb406551ce 03f6f67180e155035fef8fbedd625e19364e1ac0 && git checkout -B drift-repro cfe3563003933662ffc785e2b10041bb406551ce && git merge --no-ff 03f6f67180e155035fef8fbedd625e19364e1ac0

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json cfe3563003933662ffc785e2b10041bb406551ce
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs cfe3563003933662ffc785e2b10041bb406551ce` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

- **Form:** draft to `main`. The whole card lands here under `Fixes #31796`. `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, because plugin-audit's `sys_audit_log.action` option set gains `credential_use` (seat answer 6733054769). `Metadata-protocol: none`, because the option set is plugin-audit's own, not spec. Patch changeset for plugin-audit and plugin-auth.
- **Ruling followed: A.** plugin-audit recognises the two existing last-use stamps in an `afterUpdate` hook: `sys_api_key` from core's shared admission, and `sys_oauth_consent` from plugin-auth's MCP stamper. It writes one `credential_use` row per credential per window, carrying the principal, credential id, kind, organization and `used_at`. The row never holds the key, the token, a hash or a prefix. Admission code is untouched. Source IP and user agent are null here; that is #31821.
- **`skip_consent` clients:** with no consent row bound to the grant and the application row saying `skip_consent`, the stamper hands the use to the optional audit-slot member `recordCredentialUse`. This happens under the same throttle, claimed before any I/O: once per (client, user, organization) per clock hour in each process. The module note declares that several processes may each record the same hour once. No spec contract changes.
- **Pins and ablations:** 12/12 and 16/16. 7 ablations, each red at the right pin and then restored clean. plugin-audit 1237/1237, plugin-auth 4440 pass. Typecheck and eslint are clean.
- **Declared deviations:** two durability scripts register the new persist callee, the tenant-audit census is recounted 276 → 277 (doc and counts file), and the generated translation files carry the new action label. Forced test edits: the two writer-first action pins, and an optional `getAuditSink` on the plugin-auth rig.

- **Open question answered:** the CRUD mirror's unattributed `sys_api_key` / `sys_oauth_consent` update row per stamp stays as it is. It is the generic data-change record, not the credential ledger, and is out of this card. Nothing is filed.
- **Out of scope:** #31821 (client IP and user agent), already filed.
- **Landing:** ready and auto-merge in this stroke. On merge: a landing record on #31796, `pm:dispatched` removed, and the card closed by `Fixes`.
